n: Credited to David, this song captures a pilgrim’s joy when invited to go to the temple. Latter-day Saints often apply it to the joy of temple worship today.

f.w: Let us go into the house of the LORD

n: At last their feet are standing inside Jerusalem’s gates — the journey is over.
Jerusalem is built as a city ‘joined together,’ tightly knit — a picture of unity among God’s people.
Here the tribes of Israel go up, as God commanded, to give thanks to his name.

f.g: The decree or ordinance given to Israel.

n: Jerusalem was also the seat of justice, where David’s royal family judged the people.
‘Pray for the peace of Jerusalem’ — a wordplay, since ‘Jerusalem’ sounds like ‘peace’ (shalom). Those who love her will be secure.

f.w: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem

n: May peace be within your walls and security in your fortresses.
For the sake of family and friends, he blesses the city: ‘Peace be within you.’
Most of all, because God’s house is there, he will seek the city’s good. Love for God’s house becomes love for his people.

f.w: Because of the house of the LORD
